You're the one that's going to form their thoughts, their shapes, their identity. See how the evil comes up: scripture tell you of idleness cometh much evil. precepts.point: Deacon: we've allowed mass media to raise our kids, and that's a secondary thing. We've exchanged, and we fell for the trap hook, line, and sinker. Many of our people mistake feeding their kids and making sure they have clothes and a roof and they go to school as raising your kids, and it's two distinct differences.

note.label: Making the Great Red Dragon's 8th Head 'great Again'

precepts.why:
Isaiah says, “As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them.” These same kids become the neighborhood oppressors, running around with Glocks and taped-up mags and all that foolishness, and there is no man anywhere in the picture: no man with authority, no dignity, no order, no structure. Ecclesiasticus gives the charge that was missing: “Give him no liberty in his youth, and wink not at his follies.”

You have to hold those children in. You have to take that by the reins, because you are the one who is going to form their thoughts, their shape and their identity. Don’t give them liberty in their youth, and don’t wink at their follies.

Look at what happens when that is not done. They wanted to kill Julio Foolio over a rap battle: young, dumb, stupid people, wise to do evil. They used a girl’s phone to track him, bought AR-15 type weapons with brass catchers so the shells would not be left at the scene, and shot up his birthday party at a hotel. They thought they got away, but the police got every camera, the house cameras, the phone records, the tag readers and the Flock cameras, and the investigators took their time and put the pieces together. Lock, seal, smack, boom, you’re going down. Your ass is in jail and your mind is still a child. When the enticement wears off, reality seeps back in, and it usually comes with the arrest.

We have children in our nation too, some disrespectful to their parents, some who won’t listen. You don’t know what your parents are trying to save you from, and once you learn it, it may be too late to turn around. That behavior is not normal, not for our people, the royalty, and not period. And the eighth head knows this. They don’t care if it touches some of theirs; that is collateral damage. Their elite make sure their own children get the lessons they need to not fall into it. We are the only ones who eat this stuff up.

He left behind him an avenger against his enemies, and one that shall requite kindness unto his friends: meaning your son will look after your father's friends.
precepts.point: King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the tribute, and all Israel stoned him with stones, that he died., you came in to collect money? We ain't giving you nothing. And Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot to flee to Jerusalem; he said, they going to kill me next. So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Rehoboam took his father’s throne. “Though his father die, yet he is as though he were not dead: for he hath left one behind him that is like himself.” When you die, your son should be in your image. “While he lived, he saw and rejoiced in him: and when he died, he was not sorrowful.”

“He left behind him an avenger against his enemies, and one that shall requite kindness to his friends.” Your son is supposed to look after his father’s friends.

The old men who stood before Solomon were his father’s friends, and they counselled him: “If thou wilt be a servant unto this people this day, and wilt serve them, and answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be thy servants for ever.” “But he forsook the counsel of the old men”. And he was like his father in the worst way: Solomon in his old age forced the people to pay tribute to the houses of his wives’ gods, and Rehoboam said, “my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.” I am going to be worse than my father.

precepts.text: Weep bitterly a day or two for the dead, then comfort thyself for thy heaviness, for of heaviness cometh death and the heaviness of the heart breaketh strength. Stress makes a man weak: you do not want to work out, you eat more, you gain weight, and eventually it is death. Brothers, do not let stress keep you from the work; some of you have sat in regular clothes for years with the prophecies coming to pass. What is keeping you back is sin. Examine yourself. The Most High is doing his part; it is time we do ours.
precepts.point: Love thine own soul, comfort thy heart, and remove sorrow far from thee, for sorrow hath killed many. Captain Shamai has pushed working out for five years; a brother lost serious weight only by changing his diet and walking an hour a day around his neighborhood. Walk before you go in the house after a twelve-hour shift, because once you are inside you have more excuses than a crackhead.

note.label: The Storm Before the Kingdom

precepts.why:
“Give not over thy mind to heaviness.” Every class is preparing you for what is coming: rent, mortgage, food and gas are going sky-high, ten dollars a gallon, and you will not get a raise. Can you change it? Then why worry about it? “Love thine own soul, and comfort thy heart, remove sorrow far from thee: for sorrow hath killed many.” Stress and worry have killed many, and you are no different.

Sirach shows what heaviness does: “Weep bitterly, and make great moan, and use lamentation, as he is worthy, and that a day or two, lest thou be evil spoken of: and then comfort thyself for thy heaviness.” This is speaking of when somebody passes: mourn, and then comfort yourself.

“For of heaviness cometh death, and the heaviness of the heart breaketh strength.” Heaviness, stress, brings death. And the heaviness of the heart breaks strength: stress makes a man weak. When you are stressed, you don’t want to work out, you don’t want to go to work. Some people eat more; you gain weight, you become fat and sloppy, you lay back, and eventually it is death.

So, brothers, do not let stress wear you down so that you don’t want to do the Most High’s work. Some of you have sat here five or six years in regular clothes. You see the prophecies coming to pass, wars all over the place, World War III a matter of time, and you still sit there. What are you waiting for? What is keeping you back is sin. Examine yourself.

When correction comes, push harder; prove to Messiah you are still in the fight. Don’t hold grudges and keep to yourself, because that is when Satan messes with your head. A merry heart makes a cheerful countenance, but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken. The Most High is doing his part. It is time we do ours.

precepts.point: A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last, and he that loveth danger shall perish therein. We have to prophesy against the idolatry and come out of Christmas, Valentine's Day and the rest that God never gave us.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
The Lord clothed us and named us, yet even in 2026 our people are still worshiping the devil, giving gifts to the sea goddess. And we wonder why America is going down there stealing presidents, starving people out and destabilizing countries. “A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last; and he that loveth danger shall perish therein.” We have to prophesy against the idolatry and come up out of this foolishness: Christmas, Valentine’s Day, which a lot of our people celebrated. That has nothing to do with us. God did not give that to us.

Sirach shows where stubbornness is dealt with: “Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn, and be disobedient unto thee, and so bring sorrow to thine heart.”

That is why we teach God’s laws the way we do. We are not going to the left or to the right with any of you. We are not playing games, because we know why we got over here. We know how we got here: through stubbornness. So if we want to be delivered, we have to wake up.

Judges shows how Israel gets down: “when the judge was dead, that they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them”, and “they ceased not from their own doings, nor from their stubborn way.” When there is no leader in place, when the officer, the captain, the deacon or the bishop isn’t there, they go back to their lonesome. If you cannot uphold righteousness when nobody is looking, that is your future: damnation, judgment, destruction. A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last.

precepts.text: Remove sorrow far from thee, for sorrow hath killed many; losing Benjamin would have killed Jacob.
precepts.point: Ye shall bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave: Jacob never got over Joseph being taken away. Sorrow kills; give not over thy mind to heaviness, for the gladness of the heart is the life of man, and losing Benjamin also would have brought their father to the grave.

note.label: Genesis 44: The Cup in Benjamin's Sack and Judah's Surety

precepts.why:
“Give not over thy mind to heaviness, and afflict not thyself in thine own counsel. The gladness of the heart is the life of man, and the joyfulness of a man prolongeth his days. Love thine own soul, and comfort thy heart, remove sorrow far from thee: for sorrow hath killed many, and there is no profit therein.”

Sorrow kills. Jacob never got over Joseph being taken away: “Surely he is torn in pieces; and I saw him not since.” Of the two sons Rachel bare him, the eleventh and the twelfth, one was gone, and losing Benjamin also would have brought their father to the grave: “ye shall bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave.” The gladness of the heart is the life of man, and taking the last of it from Jacob would have killed him.

precepts.point: The same way we make haste to stop the different sins, be quick to change the diet. If we make haste to change those things, the Most High will also keep away that continual sickness, the diabetes and everything causing our limbs to be cut off just to live.

note.label: Joshua 14: Caleb Wholly Followed the Most High

precepts.why:
“Health and good estate of body are above all gold, and a strong body above infinite wealth. There is no riches above a sound body, and no joy above the joy of the heart. Death is better than a bitter life or continual sickness.” Caleb had that sound body at eighty-five, with his strength “for war, both to go out, and to come in.”

Do not spend your years on the earth in continual sickness. Leadership has been pushing that we all need to take care of our bodies and our health. A lot of us deal with gluttony even though it is not a topic we talk about all the time; cut down a little what you eat and eat better food.

precepts.point: Discipline must start in the youth. If you wait until twelve or thirteen to begin, it is over, or you will have a very difficult time.

note.label: Proverbs 19: Discipline, the Fear of the Lord, and Servitude

precepts.why:
“Chasten thy son while there is hope, and let not thy soul spare for his crying.” There is a window when chastening still has hope in it, and a father is not to hold back because the child cries.

Ecclesiasticus says the same and says when: “Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn, and be disobedient unto thee, and so bring sorrow to thine heart.” Discipline must start in the youth. If you wait until twelve or thirteen to begin, it is over, or you will have a very difficult time; by then he has waxed stubborn and disobedient, and the sorrow comes to your own heart.

Esau has continually tried to take away our ability to rightfully punish our children and bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord. The law gives that right to the parent, and it gives it while there is hope.

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

precepts.why:
That’s Satan on your brain, causing you to think like that. If you were meditating in the scriptures and you believed the scriptures, you would put the thoughts Satan is giving you to the side. “Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” The devil comes with them evil thoughts, having you thinking them evil things, like the picture of all these demons around you trying to pull you in every direction. The Bible says resist the devil and he will flee.

How do you resist him? By standing strong in his word and understanding your purpose: that you’re an Israelite, put on this earth to serve God and to serve God’s people.

“Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.” It’s time to stop being double-minded. It’s already been proven: as read earlier, our enemies shall be found liars unto us, meaning they can’t lie to us no more and tell us we’re not the Israelites. We got too much evidence; the truth is out here now. So you know who you are; now it’s time to get yourself together.

note.label: Buck Breaking and Building God's People

precepts.why:
One sister came in to say shalom with a big tongue ring in her mouth. I said what the hell is that in your mouth? Get that out of your damn mouth. She said she’d been with the body three years and nobody said nothing to her. Well, today is your day. She asked, is there a scripture? Because that elicits whoredom.

“Hear ye the word which the Lord speaketh unto you, O house of Israel: Thus saith the Lord, Learn not the way of the heathen”. That’s not our custom, sister, to put a damn ball bearing on your tongue. Take it out your mouth. You might get away with that with other congregations; I’m not the one.

note.label: HELP | Healing Emotionally Lost People

precepts.why:
“A merry heart doeth good like a medicine”. A merry mind does good like a medicine. Being joyful and glad, especially on the Most High’s high holy days, is medicine to your mind and your spirit. So when you come in here, shake the depressed spirit off and leave it at the door. You may be stressed out, with bills and things going on in your personal life, but once you come through these doors you forget them, even if for a little moment.

“But a broken spirit drieth the bones.” A broken spirit, a broken mind, a broken brother or sister: it dries up your bones and causes sickness. So we have to come out of that thing. And you are not alone: we have congregations throughout the face of the earth. Israel is growing, and we are not small anymore.

This is the gladness of the heart that Ecclesiasticus 30:22 calls the life of man.

note.label: HELP | Healing Emotionally Lost People

precepts.why:
“For of heaviness cometh death”. Heaviness is depression and distress, and it can cause you to die: internal organ failure, and thoughts of suicide. Brothers have thoughts of suicide because they let the depression get to them.

“And the heaviness of the heart breaketh strength.” It makes you weak. It makes you not want to eat, not want to congregate, not want to come around the brothers anymore. That is why Ecclesiasticus 30:21 says, give not over thy mind to heaviness. So how do we get our strength, our healing, our help?

note.label: HELP | Healing Emotionally Lost People

precepts.why:
This was spoken on a high holy day, and we just kept the feast of tabernacles. “Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet”: at tabernacles we were eating and drinking as a body, a congregation, around the bishops and deacons, the captains and officers, the tribes set up, everywhere shalom. It was healing and nurturing to the spirit: the unity, the healing of a nation. Tents open and nothing lost, no fights, no arguments, all joy: a glimpse of what the future will look like for us.

“And send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared”: single brothers and single sisters; nobody went hungry at tabernacles. There was a spirit of giving and sharing: what is mine is yours. “For this day is holy unto our Lord”: the feast day is holy unto the Lord.

“Neither be ye sorry”. We have to stop feeling sorry for ourselves. The day of the Lord is a beautiful thing, and being an Israelite while we see the Most High moving and the nations at war, all for the deliverance of the nation of Israel, is a beautiful thing. “For the joy of the Lord is your strength.” It brings joy to the Most High’s heart when we come together, and that is our strength. Even when you are distressed and depressed, shake it off, because it can make you sick. That is the gladness and joyfulness of Ecclesiasticus 30:22 that prolongs our days.

note.label: The Last Man Standing

precepts.why:
When it defines you, it also limits your growth. “And the Spirit of God came upon Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, which stood above the people, and said unto them, Thus saith God, Why transgress ye the commandments of the Lord, that ye cannot prosper?” See that: why transgress ye, that ye cannot prosper. “Because ye have forsaken the Lord, he hath also forsaken you.” When we go against the Lord, he will forsake us, and things will go wrong.

It also brings fear and anxiety, making a person hesitant to take risks or to step out of their comfort zone and try new things. When we go to camp we see which brothers are fearful: scared to stand before an audience, thinking somebody is going to punch them in the face, with no confidence in their speaking.

note.label: The Last Man Standing

precepts.why:
Letting a bad situation define you also affects your work life. “A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.” A good name means a good reputation. You want a good reputation in this truth; you want to build up your character.

Bad situations, conflicts with co-workers, a toxic work culture or personal stress lead to decreased productivity, increased stress, burnout and low morale. We see it in here: when we ask certain brothers or sisters to do things and their productivity goes lower and lower, we know something is going on in your spirit.

note.label: The Last Man Standing

precepts.why: It also affects your relationships. “He that troubleth his own house shall inherit the wind: and the fool shall be servant to the wise of heart.” When you let things define you and you can't overcome them, it will affect your relationship, your marriage.

note.label: The Last Man Standing

precepts.why: “Unless a man hold himself diligently in the fear of the Lord, his house shall soon be overthrown.” It affects your relationships and your marriage. Bad situations bring conflict and tension, disagreements and friction; they erode trust (there were something like eight cases of adultery in the past two weeks); they bring emotional distance and isolation, where a person withdraws and cannot open up or be present for their loved ones; they bring stress, and they hinder communication. There is a lot of that going on.

It’s going to get hard. It’s hard to lose weight; it ain’t easy to go to the gym every single day, but you got to push. Thirty days is how you develop a habit (some people say 90, some say 60, I say 30). Go to the gym consistently every day of the week, besides the Sabbath and any high holy days, and your body starts to crave it: I got to build on this momentum. If I miss three, four days in a row I feel horrible, and when I go back it’s hard: damn man, I was lifting this two weeks ago and now it’s a struggle, because I missed so much time. You have to push yourself.

It ain’t easy to stay committed to education either. Some of you work a full-time job, you’re a parent, you’re in this truth and you’re in school. But you got to say, look, I got a purpose, I got a goal, I got to meet it. You got to remove that heaviness from your mind, that doubt from your mind.

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

points: “The gladness of the heart is the life of man, and the joyfulness of a man prolongeth his days”: why? Because you have a healthy heart, which is your mind.

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

points: “Love thine own soul”: the same thing just read in the Proverbs, love your own soul. “And comfort thy heart, remove sorrow far from thee: for sorrow hath killed many”: a lot of people done died from sorrow, because their brain ain’t working like it’s supposed to.

“And there is no profit therein”: there’s no profit in sitting around sad and sick all the time. You’re doing that because you don’t have a purpose, or at least you don’t know your purpose. The Bible is giving us clear instructions on how to deal with these things.

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

points: “Health and good estate of body are above all gold, and a strong body above infinite wealth.” A strong body above infinite wealth, brothers: you got to exercise, you got to eat right. The only way they’re going to get right is when we get right: when we start losing the weight and getting in shape, bulking up or leaning out, whatever it is, they’re going to get right.

Get rid of the junk food. A Dorito chip put up under a microscope shows little parasites and bugs; once they put that stuff in a bag they just leave it there, and it develops parasites and bacteria, and then you’re feeding it to your kids and wondering why your kid is acting a fool, why their brain ain’t working right. Be mindful of that: you got to eat right, and you got to teach your family to eat right.

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

points: “There is no riches above a sound body, and no joy above the joy of the heart.”

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

points: “Death is better than a bitter life or continual sickness.”

note.label: Soul Searchers Looking for a Purpose

points: Frederick Douglass made a profound statement: ‘It is easier to build strong children than to repair broken men.’ Sisters, I know you got it hard, or you think you got it hard, but it’s easier to build strong children, because they’re moldable. Our job is harder, brothers: as teachers, it’s not that easy to repair broken men. We’re broken mentally, in spirit; you men and you women are broken. We come in with broken minds, conformed to this world, and now we want to be transformed. That takes time, that takes patience, that takes practice, practicing God’s laws in our lives. What is the formula to repair broken men? It’s the same formula you use to build strong children.

“He that maketh too much of his son shall bind up his wounds”: brothers, you teachers, the same way the woman is not to make too much over her child, don’t make too much over these men and women that are coming in. “And his bowels will be troubled at every cry.” You know when a child trips, the mother goes, and what did the father say? Let that boy cry, let him cry. So likewise when brothers go through their adversity, as teachers we’re not to jump to their defense. They got to go through that. You must cry.

note.label: Buck Breaking and Building God's People

points: “An horse not broken becometh headstrong: and a child left to himself will be wilful.” A man or a woman left to themselves will be wilful, wilful to commit sin. It’s the same formula.

note.label: Buck Breaking and Building God's People

points: “Cocker thy child, and he shall make thee afraid”: the same thing with broken spirits, broken minds. “Play with him, and he will bring thee to heaviness”: he’ll bring you to sorrow.

note.label: Buck Breaking and Building God's People

points: “Laugh not with him”: don’t joke around so much with your child, just like don’t joke around too much with these men and women that are coming in, “lest thou have sorrow with him”, lest you have sorrow with them, “and lest thou gnash thy teeth in the end.”

note.label: Buck Breaking and Building God's People

points: “Give him no liberty in his youth”: just like you give a child no liberty in their youth, when you men and women come in we’re not to give you liberty; give you something to do. “And wink not at his follies”: your follies are your sins; we’re not to wink at your sins. Some congregations see the sin in the men and women. It’s not hatred, it’s love. You see it, and you going to make believe you didn’t see it? No, I saw what I saw.

note.label: Buck Breaking and Building God's People

points: “Bow down his neck while he is young”: young in age, and young in spirit for you adults. “And beat him on the sides while he is a child”: now we know we can’t put our hands on you, but we can put you out; we can put some kind of judgment on you. And that’s not to destroy you; it’s meant to build you, to make you recollect where you went wrong. “Lest he wax stubborn, and be disobedient unto thee”: if we don’t do that, you will wax stubborn and become disobedient unto God’s laws, “and so bring sorrow to thine heart.”

note.label: Buck Breaking and Building God's People

points: “Chastise thy son, and hold him to labour”: we got to hold you men and women to labour, “lest his lewd behaviour be an offence unto thee”, because if we don’t hold you to labour you will become lewd in the congregations. I hope you captains understand what I’m going over.

note.label: Buck Breaking and Building God's People

points: “Give not over thy mind to heaviness”. Heaviness is depression and distress. “And afflict not thyself in thine own counsel”: that is you separating yourself, straying from the pack, from the body, from the pride. You have to stay within the congregation, because that is where the help is and where you are strongest. When we are together: go to the ant, thou sluggard, and be wise. Giving your mind to heaviness and afflicting yourself in your own counsel will lead to depression, stress and distress.

note.label: HELP | Healing Emotionally Lost People

points: “The gladness of the heart is the life of man”. That is why we go into the scriptures, to Deuteronomy 7:6, Genesis 32:28, Luke 1:68: they are supposed to bring us gladness and joy. Why do you think we have so many high holy days? Because we come from trauma and depression, and the Most High is bringing us out of it. The joy of the Lord is your strength, so we have to gather ourselves together. “And the joyfulness of a man prolongeth his days”: joyfulness prolongs our days.

note.label: HELP | Healing Emotionally Lost People

points: “Love thine own soul”. You have to love yourself; no one is going to love you more than you love yourself. “And comfort thy heart”: comfort your mind. The things you did in the past, put them behind you and do not dwell on them. “Remove sorrow far from thee: for sorrow hath killed many”. Stress breaks your body down and brings affliction: heart failure, organ failure, cancer, diseases come from stress and sorrow.

“And there is no profit therein.” There is no profit in always being down, always depressed, separating yourself. You have to be joyful and glad, and you do that by coming around the body. When brothers are together we build, we go over scriptures, we laugh, we joke, we console one another. After the high holy days, after camp and powerful teaching, you are forced up at five in the morning in the dark to go work for Esau or the other nations, and wait two weeks to get paid for your labor for the enemy. That is depressing. You come out of it by coming around the body and building yourselves up in your most holy faith.

note.label: HELP | Healing Emotionally Lost People

points: When something bad happens you have three choices: you can let it define you, you can let it destroy you, or you can let it make you durable. The three Ds: define, destroy, durable. You have to pick which one.

When you let bad things define you: “Give not over thy mind to heaviness, and afflict not thyself in thine own counsel.” Sometimes bad things happen and you let that destroy your world, or things do not go the way you planned and you let that define you, and everything is wrong.

It causes low self-esteem, a negative self-image: negative self-talk, focusing on your flaws and exaggerating imperfections, feeling unworthy or inadequate, avoiding challenges, hesitant to take risks out of self-doubt. When you let a bad situation define you, you do not see yourself in a good light. You run from situations, because you feel you can't do it, you can't overcome, you just ain't right, you're no damn good.

note.label: The Last Man Standing

points: Back then children got a whipping. We integrated and wanted to start disciplining our kids like Esau. No, discipline your kids the way God said to. And it is not the crazy, extreme stuff.

“He that loveth his son causeth him oft to feel the rod”, the rod of correction and rebuke, “that he may have joy of him in the end.” So when he grows up he is not a drug dealer; he has a sense of morals and the fear of God.

note.label: State of Decay

points: “He that chastiseth his son shall have joy in him, and shall rejoice of him among his acquaintance.”

note.label: State of Decay

points: “He that teacheth his son grieveth the enemy”. It is not beating him to a pulp out of frustration because you feel you cannot control him; that is abuse. It is the rod and correction, and teaching.

The other nations understood this, and that is why integration was pushed on our people. That sister, Barbara Sizemore, became a teacher and a writer, one of the first black women to head the public school system of a major city, Washington DC. Where did she see that? From her third and seventh grade teachers, the image in front of her. He that teacheth his son grieveth the enemy, and integration was set to destroy and dismantle all of that. “And before his friends he shall rejoice of him.”

note.label: State of Decay

points: “Though his father die, yet he is as though he were not dead”. It is as though the father did not even die, because his son comes up in his stead. Everything the father had he poured into his son, and now the son is a replica and an example of his father: “for he hath left one behind him that is like himself.” That is what we saw in 2 Maccabees 7; you know that household had a father in it, and the mother was teaching them.
“While he lived, he saw and rejoiced in him”.

note.label: State of Decay
